blockers: Foreign-key surrogate key construction between silver_customers and silver_orders/silver_order_items is brittle and ambiguous: the hash-based customer_pk_ref/order_pk_ref logic must exactly mirror whichever PK strategy WG1 selects, but the plan doesn’t define a single shared implementation or config flag. Divergence between models would silently destroy referential integrity and is hard to detect upfront.

Incremental loading + deduplication is underspecified for late-arriving or backfilled rows: dedup is described conceptually over the full RAW set, but the incremental pattern only processes rows with watermark > last_successful_watermark and merges by PK. This will not re-evaluate older natural-key groups when late duplicates arrive, breaking determinism and potentially leaving non-canonical records in SILVER.

Quarantine handling for FK violations is not concretely wired into the execution plan: quarantine targets (AwsDataCatalog.test_silver_quarantine.*) and flags are described, but it’s unclear whether they are separate models, views, or side-effect writes from the core models, and how they participate in batching, contracts, and validation. This ambiguity risks non-executable or non-idempotent implementations.

Validation configuration dependencies (config.* thresholds, exception configs, FK soft/hard thresholds, freshness lags) are heavily relied on but not modeled as explicit artifacts or dependencies. Without clear definition of where these live, how they’re versioned, and how they’re made available at runtime, initial runs can fail or behave inconsistently across environments.

Row-count ratio tests require access to raw_row_count and last_successful_row_count, but the plan doesn’t specify how these metrics are captured and persisted across runs (e.g., dedicated audit tables, metadata models). Without a concrete mechanism, these validations cannot be implemented deterministically and will either be skipped or cause runtime failures.
fixes: Introduce a single configuration switch and/or shared UDF for PK strategy per entity (e.g., customers_pk_mode=natural|surrogate, orders_pk_mode=natural|surrogate), and have all models derive customer_pk_ref/order_pk_ref through this shared abstraction instead of re-implementing the hash logic in multiple places.

Redesign the incremental strategy to ensure deduplication is performed over all rows for each natural key affected in a run: either periodically run full rebuilds, or on each incremental load pull the full history for any natural keys present in the new increment and re-derive the canonical record set before merging.

Define explicit quarantine models (or views) in the plan with their own sql_model + schema_contract + validate where appropriate, including naming, write pattern (append vs rebuild), and their position in the batch and dependency graph so that FK-violation handling is executable and idempotent.

Add an explicit "validation_config" artifact or table to the plan, detailing how config.* thresholds and exception records are stored, versioned, and read at runtime, and declare all cleanse/validate tasks as depending on this config being materialized.

Specify a concrete mechanism for persisting and accessing raw_row_count and last_successful_row_count (e.g., per-run audit tables populated by a pre-validation profiling step), and wire validate suites to read from these sources so row-count ratio tests are implementable and deterministic.

DESIGN MEMO: SILVER / CLEANSE PLAN FOR RAW CUSTOMERS AND ORDERS (REVISED)

1. GOALS

Primary goal  
Build a deterministic, incrementally maintainable SILVER (cleanse) layer for the three discovered RAW tables, producing clean, typed, deduplicated, and relationally consistent entities suitable for downstream GOLD models and BI.

Specific objectives  
- Normalize and standardize customer and order data:
  - Enforce stable primary keys, data types, and basic business rules.
  - Standardize key fields (emails, timestamps, statuses, numeric measures, currencies).
- Preserve fidelity to RAW:
  - No business aggregation; only cleaning, conforming, and deduplication.
  - Maintain row-level traceability back to RAW tables.
- Establish explicit contracts and validations:
  - Schema contracts that define column names, types, constraints, and relationships.
  - Automated validation suites that gate deployments and loads.

Scope  
- RAW inputs (bounded and immutable for this plan):
  - AwsDataCatalog.test_raw.raw_customers
  - AwsDataCatalog.test_raw.raw_orders
  - AwsDataCatalog.test_raw.raw_order_items
- No pre-existing models; design relies on SQL schema discovery.
- Execution plan batched in groups of up to 5 tasks. For this scope:
  - One batch containing 3 sql_models (each with its own contract + validate).


2. TARGET ENVIRONMENT AND NAMING

Canonical SILVER namespace  
- Database/catalog: AwsDataCatalog  
- Schema: test_silver  

Configuration  
- The SILVER schema is parameterized via environment/config, e.g.:
  - raw_schema: AwsDataCatalog.test_raw
  - silver_schema: AwsDataCatalog.test_silver
- All sql_models and schema_contracts will reference the SILVER schema via these configuration parameters so that:
  - Physical target for each model = `${silver_schema}.<model_name>`.


3. SOURCE ENTITIES AND ASSUMPTIONS

3.1 AwsDataCatalog.test_raw.raw_customers

Role  
- Core customer entity; may contain duplicates, inconsistent identifiers, messy email formats.

Likely fields (to be confirmed via schema discovery)  
- customer_id (string/bigint) – upstream logical customer key.
- email (string) – probed and confirmed present.
- first_name, last_name (string).
- created_at, updated_at (timestamp/string).
- status / is_active (string/boolean).
- Ingestion metadata: _ingested_at, _load_batch_id, _source_system, etc. (names to be confirmed).

Key assumptions  
- customer_id is the natural key; will be the primary candidate for PK in SILVER.
- Email is non-unique but must be standardized and quality-checked.
- Timestamps may be strings and require parsing/normalization to UTC.

3.2 AwsDataCatalog.test_raw.raw_orders

Role  
- Order header entity; one row per order, linked to a customer.

Likely fields  
- order_id (string/bigint) – natural order key.
- customer_id (string/bigint) – FK to customers (natural).
- order_ts / created_at (timestamp/string).
- order_status (string).
- currency (string).
- total_amount (numeric/decimal/string).
- Ingestion metadata as above.

Key assumptions  
- Each order belongs to exactly one customer in the business logic, though data might violate this.
- Some orders can appear without matching customers (latency, upstream issues).

3.3 AwsDataCatalog.test_raw.raw_order_items

Role  
- Order line-item entity; one row per product line within an order.

Likely fields  
- order_item_id (string/bigint) – if present, potential line PK.
- order_id (string/bigint) – FK to orders.
- line_number (int) – line index, if order_item_id is absent.
- product_id / sku (string).
- quantity (numeric/int/string).
- unit_price (numeric/decimal/string).
- line_amount (numeric/decimal/string).
- Ingestion metadata.

Key assumptions  
- Referential integrity to orders is desired in SILVER.
- Numeric fields may be strings or messy and require casting and validation.


4. CLEANSE LAYER DESIGN PRINCIPLES

- One SILVER model per RAW table:
  - silver_customers from raw_customers.
  - silver_orders from raw_orders.
  - silver_order_items from raw_order_items.
- Deterministic and idempotent:
  - Given the same RAW snapshot, repeated runs produce byte-equivalent SILVER outputs.
  - Deduplication uses explicit, ordered tie-break rules.
- Minimal but strict cleaning:
  - Enforce PK/unique, types, and not-null on core identifiers and timestamps where business-appropriate.
  - Standardize email, currency, timestamps, and statuses.
- Traceability:
  - Retain original keys and ingestion metadata for lineage.
  - Keep raw fields alongside cleaned ones where helpful (e.g., raw_email vs email_clean).
- Defensive design:
  - Use try_cast-like patterns and quality flags instead of failing hard at first cast error.
  - Explicitly flag or quarantine problematic records (e.g., FK violations, bad metrics) rather than silently dropping them.


5. TASK INVENTORY (WHAT WILL BE AUTHORED)

Core sql_models (3)  
1) sql_model: silver_customers  
   - Source: AwsDataCatalog.test_raw.raw_customers  
   - Target: AwsDataCatalog.test_silver.silver_customers  
   - Purpose: Clean, deduplicated customer entity with standardized email and timestamps.

2) sql_model: silver_orders  
   - Source: AwsDataCatalog.test_raw.raw_orders  
   - Target: AwsDataCatalog.test_silver.silver_orders  
   - Purpose: Clean order headers, with deterministic PKs, normalized timestamps/currencies/statuses, and a reference to silver_customers.

3) sql_model: silver_order_items  
   - Source: AwsDataCatalog.test_raw.raw_order_items  
   - Target: AwsDataCatalog.test_silver.silver_order_items  
   - Purpose: Clean order line items, with stable PK, numeric fields cleaned, and referential integrity checks to silver_orders.

For each sql_model, we will also author:
- One schema_contract:
  - Defines columns, types, PKs, FKs, and constraints.
- One validate suite:
  - Defines tests for PK uniqueness, not-null, FK coverage, numeric and temporal sanity, row-count expectations.

Total authored artifacts  
- 3 sql_models  
- 3 schema_contracts  
- 3 validate definitions  

All 9 artifacts are executed logically in a single batch (≤5 core tasks; contracts and validates are attached to each model in orchestration).


6. CHECKLIST REQUIREMENTS PER TASK TYPE

6.1 sql_model checklist

General (all models)  
- No SELECT *; explicit, ordered column list.
- Cast all columns to stable types:
  - Use try_cast (or equivalent) where data quality is uncertain.
- Use snake_case naming consistently:
  - Cleaned fields with `_clean` suffix where the raw field is preserved.
- Keep ingest and lineage columns:
  - e.g., raw_ingested_at, raw_load_batch_id, raw_source_table.
- Implement cleaning in clear stages using CTEs:
  - raw_base → typed_casts → standardized_values → deduped_output.
- Implement deterministic dedup using window functions:
  - row_number() over partition by natural key and ordered by defined tie-break columns.

6.1.1 silver_customers

Primary key and surrogate logic  
- Candidate natural key: raw customer_id.
- SILVER PK column: customer_pk (string).
  - If profiling confirms customer_id is unique (after dedup logic):  
    - customer_pk = cast(customer_id as string).
  - If customer_id is not unique or missing:
    - Introduce surrogate key:
      - customer_sk = md5(concat_ws('|', cast(customer_id as string), email, created_at_raw, coalesce(updated_at_raw, created_at_raw))).
      - Use customer_sk as PK and for downstream FKs.
    - Retain customer_id as a non-unique natural key.

Deduplication rule (if duplicates by natural key)  
- Partition: by customer_id (or customer_sk input set if natural key is missing).
- Order (from most to least preferred):
  1) updated_at_clean desc
  2) created_at_clean desc
  3) raw_ingested_at desc
  4) raw_load_batch_id desc
  5) hash_tiebreak desc, where:
     - hash_tiebreak = md5(concat_ws('|', all selected raw columns as strings))
- Keep row_number = 1.  
This ordering ensures deterministic selection, even when timestamps are tied.

Email cleaning  
- email_clean = lower(trim(email_raw)).
- is_email_valid:
  - Simple pattern check, e.g. contains '@' and a '.' after '@' and no spaces.
- Optionally maintain email_raw for traceability.

Status normalization  
- Map variants to canonical upper-case values:
  - ACTIVE, INACTIVE, BLOCKED, UNKNOWN, etc.
- status_clean derived via CASE expression on trimmed, lower(email_raw or status_raw).

Timestamp handling  
- created_at_clean = try_parse_timestamp(created_at_raw) in UTC.  
- updated_at_clean = try_parse_timestamp(updated_at_raw) in UTC.  
- timestamp_parse_issue flag:
  - is_timestamp_issue = 1 if both created_at_clean and updated_at_clean are null while raw fields are non-null.

Null-handling policy  
- Rows with null natural key (customer_id) are allowed only if:
  - We generate a surrogate (customer_sk) and set is_anonymous = true.
- If both customer_id and any reasonable surrogate attributes (email, created_at) are null:
  - Route to quarantine_customers (see FK/quarantine policy) and exclude from main silver_customers.

6.1.2 silver_orders

Primary key and surrogate logic  
- Candidate natural key: order_id.
- SILVER PK column: order_pk (string).
  - If order_id is unique after dedup:
    - order_pk = cast(order_id as string).
  - If not unique or missing:
    - order_sk = md5(concat_ws('|', cast(order_id as string), customer_id, order_ts_raw, total_amount_raw)).
    - Use order_sk as PK.

Foreign key to customers  
- customer_pk_ref (string):
  - If customer_id is valid and we used natural customer_pk:
    - customer_pk_ref = cast(customer_id as string).
  - If customers use surrogate customer_sk:
    - customer_pk_ref = md5(concat_ws('|', cast(customer_id as string), email_raw_if_present, created_at_raw_if_present)) using the exact same construction rule used in silver_customers.
- Maintain original customer_id_raw for traceability.

Deduplication rule  
- Partition: by order_id (or by surrogate-needing composite if order_id weak).
- Order:
  1) order_ts_clean desc
  2) raw_ingested_at desc
  3) raw_load_batch_id desc
  4) hash_tiebreak desc (md5 over selected raw columns)
- Keep row_number = 1.

Timestamps  
- order_ts_clean = try_parse_timestamp(order_ts_raw or created_at_raw) in UTC.
- Temporal sanity:
  - Mark is_ts_future_issue = 1 if order_ts_clean > run_date + 7 days.

Numeric fields  
- total_amount_clean = try_cast(total_amount_raw as decimal(18,2)).
- is_amount_suspicious = 1 if:
  - total_amount_clean < 0
  - OR total_amount_clean is null while total_amount_raw is non-null.

Status and currency normalization  
- order_status_clean:
  - Map variants to canonical uppercase: PENDING, PAID, SHIPPED, CANCELLED, REFUNDED, etc.
- currency_clean:
  - upper(trim(currency_raw)).
  - is_currency_valid flag if it matches a maintained ISO 4217-like whitelist.

6.1.3 silver_order_items

Primary and natural key strategy  
- Preferred PK:
  - If order_item_id exists and is unique: order_item_pk = cast(order_item_id as string).
- Fallback PK (composite):
  - (order_pk_ref, line_number_clean) if:
    - line_number is present and stable.
- If neither unique order_item_id nor stable (order_id, line_number) pair exists:
  - order_item_sk = md5(concat_ws('|', cast(order_id as string), product_id, quantity_raw, unit_price_raw, line_amount_raw, line_number_raw)).
  - Use order_item_sk as PK and keep order_id + line_number as soft natural keys.

Foreign key to orders  
- order_pk_ref:
  - If orders use natural order_pk = order_id:
    - order_pk_ref = cast(order_id as string).
  - If orders use surrogate order_sk:
    - order_pk_ref = md5(concat_ws('|', cast(order_id as string), customer_id_if_present, order_ts_raw_if_present, total_amount_raw_if_present)) with the same construction rule used in silver_orders.

Numeric fields  
- quantity_clean = try_cast(quantity_raw as decimal(18,4) or int if clearly integral).
- unit_price_clean = try_cast(unit_price_raw as decimal(18,4)).
- line_amount_clean:
  - prefer try_cast(line_amount_raw as decimal(18,4)).

Destination MUST NOT already exist (no implicit overwrite)
If expected_sha256 is provided, it MUST match the current source file sha256

top_level_args.expected_sha256: optional string (checked against the source file content)

rules: Provide patch_text only (legacy patch primitives are not allowed)

patch_text MUST start with '@@' and MUST NOT include git file headers (---/+++), diff --git preamble, or diffy-style headers (--- original / +++ modified)

top_level_args.patch_text: string (Cursor/Aider hunks-only unified diff; starts with '@@'; no file headers)

output_fields.name: __all_source_columns__
output_fields.expression: Pass through all raw/bronze source columns unchanged (do not drop columns); add cleaned/cast columns alongside raw as needed.
output_fields.description: Default silver contract: preserve all raw columns; do not filter/dedup in silver.

output_fields.name: customer_pk
output_fields.expression: customer_pk_expr(cast(customer_id as string), email_clean, created_at_clean, updated_at_clean, vc.customers_pk_mode)
output_fields.description: Deterministic primary key for customers derived via configured PK mode

output_fields.name: customer_id
output_fields.description: Raw upstream customer identifier

output_fields.name: email_raw
output_fields.description: Raw email as received from source

output_fields.name: email_clean
output_fields.description: Standardized lowercased and trimmed email

output_fields.name: is_email_valid
output_fields.expression: case when email_clean is not null and email_clean like '%@%.%' and email_clean not like '% %' then true else false end
output_fields.description: Flag indicating whether email_clean matches basic validity pattern

output_fields.name: first_name
output_fields.description: Raw first name from source

output_fields.name: last_name
output_fields.description: Raw last name from source

output_fields.name: status_raw
output_fields.description: Raw customer status from source

output_fields.name: status_clean
output_fields.expression: case lower(trim(status_raw)) when 'active' then 'ACTIVE' when 'inactive' then 'INACTIVE' when 'blocked' then 'BLOCKED' else 'UNKNOWN' end
output_fields.description: Canonicalized customer status

output_fields.name: created_at_clean
output_fields.description: Raw created_at parsed to UTC timestamp if possible

output_fields.name: updated_at_clean
output_fields.description: Raw updated_at parsed to UTC timestamp if possible

output_fields.name: is_timestamp_issue
output_fields.expression: case when (created_at is not null or updated_at is not null) and created_at_clean is null and updated_at_clean is null then true else false end
output_fields.description: True when raw timestamps are present but cannot be parsed into created_at_clean or updated_at_clean

output_fields.name: is_anonymous
output_fields.expression: case when customer_id is null and email_clean is not null then true else false end
output_fields.description: True when a surrogate or anonymous customer is inferred (no customer_id but email present)

output_fields.name: is_valid_pk
output_fields.expression: case when customer_pk is not null then true else false end
output_fields.description: True when customer_pk is non-null according to configured PK strategy

output_fields.name: is_valid_types
output_fields.expression: case when (created_at is null or created_at_clean is not null) and (updated_at is null or updated_at_clean is not null) then true else false end
output_fields.description: True when core type casts for key fields succeeded

output_fields.name: is_valid_business_rules
output_fields.expression: case when is_valid_pk = true and is_valid_types = true and (is_email_valid = true or email_clean is null) and is_timestamp_issue = false then true else false end
output_fields.description: True when basic business rules for customers pass (valid email if required, non-null PK, no impossible timestamps)

output_fields.name: raw_ingested_at
output_fields.description: Ingestion watermark from RAW used for incremental processing

output_fields.name: raw_load_batch_id
output_fields.description: Load batch identifier from RAW ingestion

output_fields.name: raw_source_system
output_fields.description: Source system identifier from RAW

output_fields.name: raw_source_table
output_fields.description: Fully qualified raw source table name for lineage

output_fields.name: run_id
output_fields.description: Execution run identifier injected by orchestration

output_fields.name: hash_tiebreak
output_fields.expression: md5(concat_ws('|', coalesce(cast(customer_id as string),''), coalesce(email_raw,''), coalesce(first_name,''), coalesce(last_name,''), coalesce(status_raw,''), coalesce(cast(created_at as string),''), coalesce(cast(updated_at as string),''), coalesce(cast(raw_ingested_at as string),''), coalesce(raw_load_batch_id,'')))
output_fields.description: Deterministic hash used as final deduplication tiebreak across otherwise identical records

output_fields.name: __all_source_columns__
output_fields.expression: Pass through all raw/bronze source columns unchanged (do not drop columns); add cleaned/cast columns alongside raw as needed.
output_fields.description: Default silver contract: preserve all raw columns; do not filter/dedup in silver.

output_fields.name: order_pk
output_fields.expression: order_pk_expr(cast(order_id as string), cast(customer_id as string), order_ts_clean, total_amount_clean, vc.orders_pk_mode)
output_fields.description: Deterministic primary key for orders derived via configured PK mode

output_fields.name: order_id
output_fields.description: Raw upstream order identifier

output_fields.name: customer_id
output_fields.description: Raw upstream customer identifier on the order

output_fields.name: order_ts_clean
output_fields.description: Order timestamp parsed to UTC from raw

output_fields.name: is_ts_future_issue
output_fields.expression: case when order_ts_clean is not null and order_ts_clean > arm.run_ts + interval vc.orders_allowed_future_lag day then true else false end
output_fields.description: True when order_ts_clean is more than allowed_future_lag days after run_ts according to validation_config

output_fields.name: total_amount_clean
output_fields.description: Cleaned numeric total order amount

output_fields.name: is_amount_suspicious
output_fields.expression: case when total_amount_clean < 0 then true when total_amount is not null and total_amount_clean is null then true else false end
output_fields.description: True when total_amount_clean is negative or failed cast while raw value present

output_fields.name: order_status_raw
output_fields.description: Raw order status from source

output_fields.name: order_status_clean
output_fields.expression: case lower(trim(order_status_raw)) when 'pending' then 'PENDING' when 'paid' then 'PAID' when 'shipped' then 'SHIPPED' when 'cancelled' then 'CANCELLED' when 'refunded' then 'REFUNDED' else 'UNKNOWN' end
output_fields.description: Canonicalized order status

output_fields.name: currency_raw
output_fields.description: Raw currency code from source

output_fields.name: currency_clean
output_fields.description: Uppercased trimmed currency code

output_fields.name: is_currency_valid
output_fields.expression: case when currency_clean in (select c.currency_code from vc.allowed_currencies c) then true else false end
output_fields.description: True when currency_clean belongs to allowed ISO-like list from validation_config

output_fields.name: customer_pk_ref
output_fields.expression: customer_pk_expr(cast(customer_id as string), email_raw_if_present, created_at_raw_if_present, updated_at_raw_if_present, vc.customers_pk_mode)
output_fields.description: Foreign-key reference to silver_customers customer_pk constructed via shared PK expression

output_fields.name: is_valid_pk
output_fields.expression: case when order_pk is not null then true else false end
output_fields.description: True when order_pk is non-null according to configured PK strategy

output_fields.name: is_valid_types
output_fields.expression: case when (order_ts is null and created_at is null) or order_ts_clean is not null then true else false end and case when total_amount is null or total_amount_clean is not null then true else false end
output_fields.description: True when core casts for order_ts_clean and total_amount_clean succeeded

output_fields.name: is_valid_business_rules
output_fields.expression: case when is_valid_pk = true and is_valid_types = true and is_ts_future_issue = false and is_amount_suspicious = false then true else false end
output_fields.description: True when basic business rules for orders pass (valid PK, types, no severe temporal or amount anomalies)

output_fields.name: is_valid_fk_customer
output_fields.expression: case when customer_pk_ref is null then false when exists (select 1 from AwsDataCatalog.test_silver.silver_customers sc where sc.customer_pk = customer_pk_ref) then true else false end
output_fields.description: True when customer_pk_ref successfully joins to an existing silver_customers record under configured FK thresholding

output_fields.name: raw_ingested_at
output_fields.description: Ingestion watermark from RAW orders used for incremental processing

output_fields.name: raw_load_batch_id
output_fields.description: Load batch identifier from RAW ingestion for orders

output_fields.name: raw_source_system
output_fields.description: Source system identifier from RAW orders

output_fields.name: raw_source_table
output_fields.description: Fully qualified raw source table name for lineage

output_fields.name: run_id
output_fields.description: Execution run identifier injected by orchestration

output_fields.name: hash_tiebreak
output_fields.expression: md5(concat_ws('|', coalesce(cast(order_id as string),''), coalesce(cast(customer_id as string),''), coalesce(cast(order_ts as string),''), coalesce(cast(created_at as string),''), coalesce(total_amount,''), coalesce(order_status,''), coalesce(currency,''), coalesce(cast(raw_ingested_at as string),''), coalesce(raw_load_batch_id,'')))
output_fields.description: Deterministic hash used as final deduplication tiebreak for orders

output_fields.name: __all_source_columns__
output_fields.expression: Pass through all raw/bronze source columns unchanged (do not drop columns); add cleaned/cast columns alongside raw as needed.
output_fields.description: Default silver contract: preserve all raw columns; do not filter/dedup in silver.

output_fields.name: order_item_pk
output_fields.expression: case when vc.order_items_pk_mode = 'order_item_id' then cast(order_item_id as string) when vc.order_items_pk_mode = 'composite' then md5(concat_ws('|', cast(order_id as string), cast(line_number as string))) else order_item_pk_expr(cast(order_item_id as string), cast(order_id as string), cast(line_number as string), cast(product_id as string), quantity_clean, unit_price_clean, line_amount_clean) end
output_fields.description: Deterministic primary key for order items based on configured PK mode

output_fields.name: line_number_clean
output_fields.description: Raw line number for the order item

output_fields.name: product_id

output_fields.name: quantity_clean
output_fields.description: Cleaned quantity for the order item

output_fields.name: unit_price_clean
output_fields.description: Cleaned unit price for the order item

output_fields.name: line_amount_clean
output_fields.description: Cleaned line amount for the order item

output_fields.name: order_pk_ref
output_fields.expression: order_pk_expr(cast(order_id as string), customer_id_if_present, order_ts_raw_if_present, total_amount_raw_if_present, vc.orders_pk_mode)
output_fields.description: Foreign-key reference to silver_orders order_pk constructed via shared PK expression

output_fields.name: is_valid_pk
output_fields.expression: case when order_item_pk is not null then true else false end
output_fields.description: True when order_item_pk is non-null under configured PK mode

output_fields.name: is_valid_types
output_fields.expression: case when (quantity is null or quantity_clean is not null) and (unit_price is null or unit_price_clean is not null) and (line_amount is null or line_amount_clean is not null) then true else false end
output_fields.description: True when numeric casts for quantity, unit_price, and line_amount succeeded or could be recomputed

output_fields.name: is_valid_business_rules
output_fields.expression: case when (quantity_clean is null or quantity_clean >= 0) and (unit_price_clean is null or unit_price_clean >= 0) and (line_amount_clean is null or line_amount_clean >= 0) then true else false end
output_fields.description: True when basic business rules for order items pass (non-negative amounts and quantities)

output_fields.name: is_valid_fk_order
output_fields.expression: case when order_pk_ref is null then false when exists (select 1 from AwsDataCatalog.test_silver.silver_orders so where so.order_pk = order_pk_ref) then true else false end
output_fields.description: True when order_pk_ref joins to an existing silver_orders record
